title: Selma bought in Paris and borrowing a Buffet
summary: Hall tells how he bought a Selma at the Paris factory during a European tour and borrowed a Buffet from Jimmy Dawson when it cracked.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, I got a, I have a new one, but it's still Albert's system. What make you use? I'm using, well this is the first time I've been using a Selma now for about a year. When we was on this tour in Europe, I bought a Selma, I went to the factory and I bought
No, it just happened so that this guy happened to have one in the factory. So, he said, I only have one. So, he went and got it. I was lucky and I got this lesson.
Do you remember what you started on? What kind of clarinet it was? Albert's system?
What do you mean? Not the name. What the make? No, I don't know what the make was.
There were a lot of them in those days. Oh, yeah. Did you ever use a buffet? Buffet?

Yeah. I was using a buffet because the one that I, this Selma client that I bought in France, it cracked on him, see? I had to have it fixed. So, it happened to, I was also using a penzamala when I was waiting at the cafe. So, Jimmy Dawson came in the place one night. So, the penzamala company gave him the clarinet, see? So, he came in and he wanted to sit down and play. I said, well, I don't know. I said, I'm using a penzamala and I said, this thing is in bad shape. So, he said, well, I have a buffet you can use and take it out to the factory and have it fixed. I used that buffet. By the way, I have that buffet now. I gave it back to him. And so, when this clarinet cracked that I have now, I went to him, he, I'm using, I still have his buffet. But, I had mine fixed and I haven't returned his buffet yet. So, I got him just before I left to come here. From where? From some fella, he's a old man, he's 80 years old, he's a retired symphony man. He had two beautiful bouffés, A and a B. I just got him, he said, I just hope somebody can get some use out of them and they're really beautiful.
